chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Fadala from Abu al-Mi'za from Sama'a from Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him) who said:
I asked him about the slaughtered animal of the Jew and the Christian, he said, "Do not approach it."
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on eating the meat of Jews and Christians in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him), the phrase 'Do not approach it' (La taqrabanna-ha) is interpreted by Shia scholars as a strong prohibition, often indicating that the meat of Jews and Christians is not considered 'good' (tayyib) as required by Quran 5:5. This view contrasts with the majority opinion that their meat is permissible, highlighting the Shia emphasis on the spiritual purity and specific conditions of slaughter beyond mere ritual validity.
